# Your Role in Research
## Who you report to The [bold]Lead Researcher[/bold] runs the laboratory. They set the research priorities, sign off on results and decide who works on what. Bring all work questions to them first.
The Lead Researcher reports to the site's management, normally the Corporate Liaison or the Division Manager. You won't usually need to deal with management directly. If they ask you about your work, answer their questions, but don't volunteer details of projects they haven't asked about.
## Academic titles Research staff hold academic titles instead of office grades. - [bold]Assistant Professor[/bold]: a qualified researcher. Every scientist starts here. - [bold]Associate Professor[/bold]: an experienced researcher, trusted to lead a line of enquiry and to supervise others. - [bold]Professor[/bold]: held by the Lead Researcher.
Promotion comes with time and results. Good, well-documented research gets noticed.
## The laboratory Your ID card opens the research areas of the site. Other staff, including most office staff, can't enter them, and they shouldn't be invited in. If someone without research access asks to come into the lab, politely refuse and let the Lead Researcher know.
## Working with other teams - [bold]Corporate Security[/bold] protect the lab and handle anything dangerous that leaves it. If they ask you to do something for your safety, do it. - [bold]Office staff[/bold] handle the site's accounts and freight. They don't need to know about your work, and you shouldn't tell them. - [bold]Colonial staff[/bold] are not Company employees. Be courteous, but never discuss your research with them.
